title: What You Wear
label: ch:ml-clothing
canDo: I can name what someone is wearing, and call it new or old.

payoff.summary: From cold: four things worn, two endings between them, and an adjective that has not moved since chapter 42.
payoff.note: Four atoms. THE EXAM POINT'S NOTE IS ACCURATE THIS TIME, and that was checked rather than assumed: the last two points worked (LEX-37, LEX-47) both had notes that overstated their gaps, so this one was token-swept first. thuni IS the only textile word taught (ML-C46-cloth), and not one garment is named -- shirt, mundu, sari, sandal, shoes, cap, glasses, watch, bag, dress and skirt all return ZERO occurrences. NO NEW GRAMMAR AT ALL, which is the point of the chapter after chapter 99 spent itself on three contrasting joins. Only two endings appear across the four words -- the half-u (mundu, cheruppu) and -i (saari, thoppi) -- and the learner owns both already, the first from paattu and the second from kali and bhangi. The frame is the attributive adjective from ML-C42: puthiya and pazhaya sit in front and do not change, which is that chapter's whole pattern applied to nouns it never had. THE GLYPH PRE-CHECK FAILED TWICE IN A NEW WAY AND WAS DEMOTED TO A SIGNAL. Its control had to be derived from the data rather than recalled, as in chapter 99 -- and then it produced FALSE NEGATIVES, refusing shirt for the chillu RR and 'to wear' for DHA, both of which appear in taught headwords already (ten and seven respectively). A check that is stricter than the rule it stands in for is not a gate; it is now used only to tell what needs a second look. shirt was dropped anyway, but on scope rather than on glyphs: mundu, saari, cheruppu and thoppi already cover all three limbs of the label -- clothing, footwear and accessories -- and a fifth clothing word adds no limb. EVERY ROMANIZATION WAS DERIVED LETTER BY LETTER, not word by word, which is the correction chapter 99 earned by getting nrttham's vowel right and the consonant beside it wrong. ca is c on sixteen headwords (the lone chaaya also lacks its macrons and is unmigrated drift, not a convention); zha is zh-with-underdot on six against two legacy spellings; NTa is NTu exactly as in chuNTu; and saari is witnessed inside samsaarikkuka's own romanization. puthiya and pazhaya were read off ML-C42's own fields rather than reconstructed.
